newsitem.title: UK: DMG says won new pension funds post-Horlick.
newsitem.headline: DMG says won new pension funds post-Horlick.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), said on Monday its fund management arm Morgan Grenfell Asset Managment (MGAM) had won new business since the sudden departure of fund manager Nicola Horlick last month.
"We have made two new business pitches on the institutional pension fund side, and we have won both of them," DMG spokesman James Murray told Reuters.
Murray said client confidentiality meant he could not disclose the names of the two institutional clients but he said the new business involved assets of more than 200 million stg.
DMG is the investment banking arm of Deutsche Bank AG.
A number of UK institutional clients said they would review their relationship with MGAM after Horlick was suspended last month as head of its UK pension fund business.
But none have yet moved their business elsewhere and some have said they will definitely keep their funds with the firm.

South London's Lambeth council said it did not anticipate any changes. "Lambeth expects to continue receiving the service from the company it has received to date and anticipates no particular changes," a council spokeswoman told Reuters.
But the Mail on Sunday newspaper reported that Lewisham council was interviewing rival fund managers to work alongside MGAM on its 350 million stg pension fund.

The paper said at least 100 million stg was expected to be transferred to another fund management firm but banking sources said the council had not made a decision. Council officials were not immediately available for comment.
